prefill.quotation: We found that the wetlands in the basin were shrinking and drying earlier in the breeding season in the late 2010s than in the late 1990s, as demonstrated elsewhere (e.g., Rashford et al. 2016).
prefill.comment: The paper links the loss of late-breeding diving ducks in the Konya Closed Basin to wetlands that shrink and dry earlier in the season, based on Landsat images of seven lakes in 1996-1998 and 2016-2018. The timing matters because a wetland that dries in mid-season can make a whole breeding season fail. The replication tests the shift in drying date with every valid Landsat scene from 1984 to 2025 at five wetlands of the basin and a stable crater lake as control.

prefill.aida: Wetlands of the Konya Closed Basin dry out earlier in the breeding season than they did in the late 1990s.

prefill.label: Konya Closed Basin wetlands shrink and dry earlier in the breeding season, late 2010s against late 1990s (Özgencil et al. 2025)
Replication of the earlier drying of Konya Closed Basin wetlands with every valid Landsat scene, 1984-2025
prefill.scope: The claim that wetlands of the Konya Closed Basin shrink and dry earlier in the breeding season in the late 2010s than in the late 1990s. In scope: the date each year at which a wetland falls to a small fraction of its spring area, compared between 1996-2000 and 2016-2020 and as a trend over 1984-2025, and whether the wetlands still fill in spring at all. Out of scope: the bird diversity results, the causes of the change, and the paper's seven lakes as such (only some of the sites overlap).
prefill.methodology: Every valid Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 scene (Landsat 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9) from 1984 to 2025 at six sites: Akgöl, Hotamış, Meke (Ramsar), Meyil, Bolluk and the crater lake Acıgöl (Karapınar) as a stable control. Site outlines from the JRC Global Surface Water maximum extent; green and near-infrared resampled onto HEALPix cells of about 49 m (depth 17, WGS84 ellipsoid, nested) before NDWI > 0; scenes kept with at least 95% valid cells. Reference area per site: median over 1984-1995 of each year's spring (March-June) maximum. Drying date: first valid scene after day 100 with water at most 10% of the reference; years that never fall that low are censored at day 366. Compared as medians of 1996-2000 against 2016-2020, as the paper's windows, and as a Theil-Sen trend over all years. Filling: share of years per decade whose spring maximum reaches half the reference.
prefill.deviation: The paper used seven Important Bird Area lakes, a few images per year in early (April-May) and late (July-August) breeding season, Level-1 products corrected in QGIS and MNDWI. This study uses six sites that only partly overlap, every valid scene, Collection 2 surface reflectance, NDWI, and a drying date rather than the mean area in two parts of the season, and extends the record to 1984-2025.

prefill.label: Konya wetlands dry earlier over 1984-2025 at three of five sites; the larger change is that they no longer fill
prefill.conclusion: Over 1984-2025 the drying date advanced at Akgöl (41 days per decade), Hotamış (24) and Meke (62), all significant; Meyil and Bolluk show no trend and the control crater lake never dries. Between the paper's windows, however, the median drying date did not advance at any site (Akgöl 164 to 165, Hotamış 121 to 119, Meke 145 to 162, Meyil 107 to 139). The reason is a larger change: the wetlands stopped filling. Akgöl filled to half its 1984-1995 spring level in every year of the 1980s, 40% of the 1990s and never since 2000; Hotamış never since 2010; Meke and Meyil in no year of the 2020s. Earlier drying is supported as a long-term trend; the dominant signal is the failure to fill.
prefill.evidence: Drying date (first scene after day 100 with water at most 10% of the 1984-1995 spring reference), Theil-Sen days per decade over 1984-2025 (95% interval): Akgöl -41.4 (-67.4 to -18.8), Hotamış -23.6 (-43.7 to -9.5), Meke -61.8 (-78.3 to -16.4), Meyil 0.0 (-9.6 to 10.0), Bolluk 0.0 (-42.5 to 26.3), Acıgöl control 0.0 (never dry). Median day of year 1996-2000 against 2016-2020: Akgöl 164/165, Hotamış 121/119, Meke 145/162, Meyil 107/139, Bolluk 236.5/366, Acıgöl 145/366. Share of years filled to half the reference, 1980s/1990s/2000s/2010s/2020s: Akgöl 1.0/0.4/0/0/0; Hotamış 1.0/0.3/0.3/0/0; Meke 1.0/1.0/1.0/0.44/0; Meyil 1.0/1.0/1.0/0.78/0; Acıgöl 1.0/0.9/1.0/1.0/1.0. Files: results/claims.json, results/fill_by_decade.csv.
prefill.limitations: The paper's seven lakes are listed in its supplement, which was not used; only some sites overlap. NDWI rather than the paper's MNDWI: it misses bright or turbid water in some scenes, notably at the crater lakes, which can set drying dates too early. A drying date is undefined in a year when a wetland does not fill, so collapse and earlier drying are hard to separate; the fill share is reported for that reason. Bolluk has few early years. No breeding-season bird data were analysed.
